niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: The Paralyzed Tendon Glitch
ideas.angle: An interactive challenge where the viewer places their palm flat on a table and tucks their middle finger under. They are then told to lift their ring finger—which is physically impossible due to shared tendons. This forces the viewer to loop the video to try again and comment their failure.

hook.en: You cannot lift your ring finger.

ideas.reason: Interactive body 'glitches' are currently the highest retention format on Shorts because they force physical participation. Similar 'impossible' body movements have recently gained millions of views by triggering high comment volume from people claiming they 'could' or 'couldn't' do it.

ideas.title: The Instant Survival Reset
ideas.angle: A high-stakes survival science video showing how splashing ice-cold water on your face instantly triggers the Mammalian Dive Reflex. It explains how this 'biological override' drops your heart rate by 25% and kills anxiety instantly. Includes a challenge to 'save this for your next panic attack'.

hook.en: Splash ice water to live longer.

ideas.reason: Biohacking and 'nervous system resets' are trending under the 'wellness' and 'survival' pillars. This specific reflex is a well-documented physiological 'glitch' that provides immediate value, driving high 'Save' and 'Share' metrics.

ideas.title: The Invisible Hand Glitch
ideas.angle: The viewer is told to scratch their left arm while looking into a mirror that hides their right arm. This triggers a 'proprioception error' where the brain feels the sensation in the wrong place. The video challenges viewers to try it with a friend or a mirror to 'break' their brain.
ideas.reason: Visual and sensory illusions that can be performed at home have a high 'Average Percentage Viewed' (APV) because viewers watch once to understand the instruction and a second time to perform it alongside the narrator.
